description: We are building VayuBudhi, an urban air quality platform combining satellite data, IoT sensors, AI forecasting, and resource optimization to turn pollution insights into action. Our interests span AI, Earth observation, and environmental sustainability. Join us to help cities make smarter decisions for cleaner air. We welcome teammates with skills in machine learning, geospatial analysis, web development, IoT, or atmospheric science.
summary:
Air pollution costs India lives, healthy years, and economic opportunity. A 2019 study in The Lancet Planetary Health attributed 1.24 million deaths in India in 2017 to air pollution—approximately one every 25 seconds. The 2025 Lancet Countdown valued premature mortality from outdoor air pollution in 2022 at US$339.4 billion, equivalent to 9.5% of GDP.

VayuBudhi turns environmental information into targeted decisions. We developed an urban air quality platform combining environmental data, local particulate sensing, forecasting, and resource optimization. It helps authorities anticipate worsening conditions, investigate likely pollution sources, and prioritize limited response resources.

Prediction uncertainty informs response planning: ambiguous signals can receive verification before larger interventions are committed. Multilingual guidance helps residents understand local conditions, while low-cost sensors complement established monitoring networks.

By connecting monitoring with action, VayuBudhi helps users determine where to investigate, what evidence supports a decision, and how available resources could respond. Our goal is earlier investigation, clearer public communication, and better informed decisions—helping cities act before pollution becomes prolonged community exposure.
details:
VayuBudhi turns urban air quality information into a practical response plan. It combines environmental data, local sensing, atmospheric science, machine learning, and resource optimization to help answer four questions: Where could air quality worsen? What might be causing it? Where should authorities investigate first? What can residents do to reduce exposure?

How it works

1. Connects environmental data with local observations

VayuBudhi brings together weather conditions, pollutant concentrations, traffic signals, and local particulate measurements. Open-Meteo provides weather and air quality information, including Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) outputs. Historical weather acquisition includes an ERA5 access pathway.

The platform also includes ingestion modules for CPCB and state pollution control board monitoring records through data.gov.in, alongside OpenAQ observations. Availability depends on credentials, station coverage, and successful data retrieval. An ESP32 and SDS011 sensor component supports local PM2.5 and PM10 monitoring.

The map’s NO₂ overlay is generated from CAMS data accessed through Open-Meteo; it is not a direct Sentinel-5P retrieval.

2. Anticipates worsening air quality

XGBoost models support forecasts at 24, 48, and 72 hours. Atmospheric features include a ventilation index calculated from boundary layer height and wind speed. This helps represent stagnant conditions in which pollutants can accumulate, connecting machine learning predictions with relevant atmospheric processes.

3. Estimates likely pollution sources and communicates uncertainty

A Random Forest model estimates likely source categories, including traffic, industry, biomass burning, and dust. MAPIE conformal prediction supports prediction sets and intervals that communicate uncertainty.

Source classification uses heuristic training labels rather than independently verified emissions-source measurements. Its outputs therefore guide investigation rather than establish responsibility for pollution. Prediction coverage must also be evaluated using representative calibration and validation data.

4. Helps prioritize investigation and response

Google OR-Tools supports resource allocation and routing for response assets such as inspectors, drones, and enforcement vehicles. The planning workflow considers pollution severity, prediction confidence, and population exposure.

Its central principle is that uncertain evidence may warrant verification before a larger intervention. This connects analytical confidence with practical decisions about where limited resources could be most useful. The routing component is a decision support capability, not evidence of an operational connection to municipal fleets.

5. Makes environmental information more accessible

The citizen advisory component translates air quality information into activity-based inhaled dose estimates and multilingual guidance. The Google Gemini API supports advisory generation, helping present complex information in more understandable language.

Exposure estimates are indicative, and generated guidance requires verification against official public health recommendations. The platform is intended to support informed decisions rather than provide individualized medical advice.

What makes VayuBudhi creative

VayuBudhi connects prediction uncertainty directly to response planning. Its contribution extends beyond displaying pollution levels: it brings monitoring, forecasting, source investigation, resource allocation, and public communication into one workflow.

A pollution signal becomes the beginning of a decision process: assess the conditions, examine the evidence, identify uncertainty, prioritize a location, and select an appropriate response. This combines atmospheric science, machine learning, geospatial visualization, and operations research around a practical urban problem.

The approach also recognizes the different roles of its inputs. Regional atmospheric models provide broader context, monitoring stations and local sensors provide location-specific observations, and predictive models help explore what may happen next.

Benefits and intended impact

VayuBudhi aims to help authorities investigate pollution earlier, allocate limited personnel more effectively, and communicate clearer guidance to residents. Its shared interface makes environmental evidence easier to explore while connecting analytical outputs with potential actions.

Low-cost sensing offers a pathway toward more distributed local monitoring. Multilingual communication can make information accessible to a wider audience, while explicit uncertainty can help users avoid treating every model output as equally reliable.

These are intended benefits. Field trials are needed to establish whether the platform improves response times, resource use, or community outcomes.

Tools and development

  • Backend and data processing: Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, pandas, and NumPy.
  • Forecasting and attribution: XGBoost, scikit-learn Random Forest, and MAPIE for conformal prediction.
  • Model interpretation: SHAP-based explanation components.
  • Resource planning: Google OR-Tools.
  • Frontend and visualization: Next.js, React, TypeScript, deck.gl, MapLibre GL JS, React Map GL, and Recharts.
  • Advisory generation: Google Gemini API.
  • Hardware: ESP32 microcontrollers and SDS011 particulate sensors.
  • Environmental and contextual integrations: Open-Meteo, CAMS, an ERA5 historical-weather access pathway, CPCB/state monitoring feeds through data.gov.in, OpenAQ, and TomTom traffic services.

Design considerations and validation

The team considered affordability, atmospheric variability, population exposure, language accessibility, and limited municipal capacity. We also distinguish measured observations, modeled environmental conditions, predictions, and simulated scenarios because each supports different conclusions.

Sensor calibration, missing-data handling, spatial representativeness, forecast evaluation, and uncertainty calibration remain essential. Source attribution requires independent validation, and operational trials are needed before routing recommendations can be relied upon in real deployments.

AI assistance and prior work

OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assisted with research, submission writing, code review, and local code changes. Machine learning supports forecasting and source attribution within the project, while Gemini supports advisory generation. AI-generated outputs do not constitute independent scientific validation.

VayuBudhi builds on prior work that placed third at The Economic Times AI Hackathon 2.0. That recognition provides background to the project.
